title: Zero-one knapsack

problem.name: Zero-one knapsack
problem.statement_latex:
Given positive integer weights $w_i$, nonnegative profits $p_i$, and capacity $W$, maximize $\sum_i p_ix_i$ subject to $x_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $\sum_iw_ix_i\leq W$. The decision version also supplies a profit target. Knapsack models budgeted selection and resource allocation.
The meet-in-the-middle comparison uses quantum coherent-memory time and classical RAM time, with polynomial bit-arithmetic costs for weights and profits.

quantum.details_latex: The capacity and profit threshold give a constant number of inequalities. Binary search over the profit range recovers the optimum with a polynomial bit-length factor. The construction requires coherent access to precomputed partial-sum and dominance-search data. QuantumTreeGenerator, a separate branch-and-bound construction, gives instance-dependent search estimates based on classical solver trees.

classical.headline_latex: $O^*(2^{n/2})$, Horowitz--Sahni meet in the middle; $O(nW)$, capacity dynamic programming.
classical.headline_text: $O^*(2^{n/2})$, Horowitz–Sahni meet in the middle; $O(nW)$, capacity dynamic programming.
classical.details_latex: The first bound enumerates partial weight-profit pairs and removes dominated pairs, using exponential memory. The second stores the best profit for each achievable capacity and is pseudopolynomial in the binary-encoded input. The smaller applicable expression supplies the comparison. If the numerical data have $B$ bits, a direct Boolean arithmetic encoding has size $O(n(B+\log n))$; any tensor-contraction bound applied to that encoding retains this dependence on $B$.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant in item count in the large-coefficient meet-in-the-middle regime, based on Grover search and amplitude amplification. Small-capacity instances have the pseudopolynomial classical comparator.

evidence.description_latex: The few-inequality upper bound is rigorous in its access model. Evidence for practical speedup from branch-and-bound estimates depends on the solver trees and implementation costs.

hardware.description_latex: Active registers include $n$ assignment qubits, $O(\log W)$ weight bits and $O(\log\sum_i p_i)$ profit bits, plus reversible workspace. The asymptotic search construction additionally needs exponential coherent memory. Useful numerical instances require fault tolerance.
